title: Bounded finite-projective model of ordinary affine sections
statement: Let $Y$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], with the derived categories of module sheaves and localized open sites [def-pc-derived-category]. Put $A=\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$. Choose a derived category of $A$-modules. Let $D$ be a cochain complex of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], zero above a natural degree $d$, with quasi-coherent terms, whose derived image is perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex]. There exist a complex $P$ of $A$-modules and integers $a,b$ such that $P^n=0$ for $n<a$ or $b<n$, each $P^n$ is finite and projective over $A$, and $Q(P)$ is isomorphic to $Q(\Gamma(Y,D))$. Here sections are applied termwise to the actual complex $D$, and $Q$ is localization at quasi-isomorphisms.

proof.text: Transport D along Y.isoSpec. The natural quasi-coherent counit gives a termwise isomorphism from associated sheaves of ordinary sections to this transported complex. Exactness of tilde shows that its homology sheaves are quasi-coherent. Transport perfectness along the same scheme isomorphism.

Apply the affine bounded-projective characterization to the transported derived object and retain the bounds, finiteness, projectivity and derived isomorphism. Compose with the termwise counit isomorphism.

Use full faithfulness of affine derived sheafification to lift the resulting isomorphism between tilde(P) and tilde(Gamma(Y,D)) to the ring derived category. Lift its inverse too; faithfulness proves both inverse identities. For the empty affine scheme the ring and its module category are zero.
